data.title: Crypto News | Short Liquidations Hit 71% as Crypto Trails a 4% Weekly Stock Rally; Monero Falls 13% on Delistings
data.description: Bitcoin rose 1.8% since midnight UTC to about $61,600 on Friday, November 27, as US markets reopened for a half-day session after Thanksgiving. Nasdaq 100 futures gained 2.6%, so bitcoin again lagged stocks. It is up 0.6% this week. If that holds through Sunday's close, it would end seven straight weekly losses, the second-longest losing streak on record. Bitcoin is still down about 20% in November, its worst month since June.Stocks and Metals Rally Into the Half-Day SessionAI infrastructure and memory chip stocks led premarket gains, extending Wednesday's advances in global markets. The S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and Dow Jones Industrial Average are each up about 4% on the week. Precious metals rebounded: silver rose about 7% to above $44 an ounce, and gold added 2.5% to above $3,670.About $7 billion of bitcoin options expired at 08:00 UTC on the largest crypto options exchange. Traders had positioned defensively ahead of the expiry.Short Liquidations Drive Bitcoin's GainCrypto liquidations fell 61% to $242 million over 24 hours, and 71% of them were short positions, compared with an even split a day earlier. Shorts made up 77% of the $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations. Bitcoin open interest barely changed, which suggests forced short covering, not new leverage, drove much of the rise.Futures trading volume fell 40% to $141.8 billion, while open interest rose 2.1% to $106.1 billion. Traders kept adding positions, but at a slower pace. Funding rates on Binance and other major exchanges cooled to roughly neutral, so long positions are no longer paying a premium. Positioning leans mildly bullish but is not crowded.Options Traders Turn Toward CallsFour of the six most traded bitcoin options over 24 hours were calls, after a day when all six were puts. Three were $62,000 to $64,000 calls expiring November 28 and 29, just above the current price, and one was a $68,000 call expiring December 4. The busiest single contract was the December 25 $50,000 put. Puts still cost more than calls, but the premium has narrowed. Ether options remain defensive: all six of the busiest contracts were puts, led by the January 29 $1,200 put.Privacy Coins Split on Delisting NewsMonero (XMR) fell 13% over 24 hours after two other exchanges said they will delist the token on November 30. They cited upcoming EU rules that bar crypto firms from offering accounts for privacy coins that hide transactions. Zcash (ZEC) rose 11% since midnight, after developers called for moving about $300 million of ZEC out of an older shielded pool. ZEC futures show crowded bullish positioning: longs made up 60% of its $13.5 million in liquidations.Altcoins Keep Pace as AI Tokens RiseAltcoins kept pace with bitcoin. The CoinDesk 80 Index rose 1.9%, and 90 of the tokens in the CoinDesk 100 were higher. DeFi led, with the CoinDesk DeFi Select Index up 4.0%. AI tokens rose with AI stocks: FET climbed 5.9% and TAO 2.4%. CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index stood at 11, in extreme fear, while its Altcoin Season Index rose to 63 from 57.

data.title: Bitcoin News | Bitcoin Nears a Death Cross: After 13 Past Signals, Losses Ranged From 0.3% to 66%
data.description: Bitcoin's short-term price trend is closing in on its long-term trend, setting up a "death cross," a chart signal technical analysts read as bearish. As of November 27, bitcoin's 50-day simple moving average was about 3.45% above its 200-day average, down from a 12% gap a month earlier. After the 13 previous death crosses, bitcoin fell further by a median of about 24%, but the declines ranged from 0.3% to 66%. Bitcoin traded near $61,541.What a Death Cross MeansA death cross forms when the 50-day moving average falls below the 200-day average. It shows that recent prices are weaker than the longer-run trend. The opposite signal, a golden cross, occurs when the 50-day average climbs back above the 200-day, and analysts read it as confirmation of an uptrend.Six Past Signals Preceded Declines of 30% or MoreCoinDesk measured each decline from bitcoin's UTC closing price on the day a death cross was confirmed to the lowest price before the next golden cross. Six signals led to declines of 30% or more. The deepest were 66% after the September 4, 2014 cross, 64% after January 14, 2022, and 59% after September 26, 2011. Three more were between 13% and 19%.Three Signals Were Near-DudsThree death crosses were followed by only shallow declines, leaving traders who sold or shorted on the signal on the wrong side of the market. Bitcoin fell just 0.3% after the September 12, 2023 cross, 2.9% after September 14, 2015, and 5.7% after April 7, 2025.These near-duds all came when bitcoin was already well below its peak, as it is now. But the 2011, 2014 and 2018 crosses also followed steep declines and still led to large further losses. Being far below the peak, on its own, doesn't predict a shallow outcome.For illustration only, a median-sized 24% decline from the current price would put bitcoin near $46,800 (calculated). The historical range is wide enough that the median says little about any single case.

data.title: Brazil’s B3 Pushes Stablecoin Launch to 2027
data.description: Brazil’s stock exchange B3 has pushed the planned launch of its Brazilian real-pegged stablecoin to the first quarter of 2027, after initially targeting a launch this year. According to Cointelegraph, local outlet Valor Econômico reported Friday that B3 is working with six major Brazilian financial institutions—Bradesco, BTG Pactual, Itaú Unibanco, Safra, Santander and XP—on the project. Named Open BRL, the stablecoin is expected to be issued by Banco B3, the exchange’s banking subsidiary, with each token backed by one real; B3 will operate its underlying technology. B3 first announced plans for a stablecoin in December 2025, targeting a launch in 2026. As recently as July, the exchange was reportedly preparing to launch a token called B3RL in the coming months, with infrastructure testing and institutional integration scheduled for August and September. B3RL was designed to be backed by reais and secured by government bonds, facilitating blockchain-based trading of stocks and fixed-income securities starting in 2027. It is unclear whether Open BRL will replace B3RL or operate alongside it. B3 also plans to begin trading tokenized shares in early 2027 using the same order book as conventional equities. In October, executive Humberto Costa reportedly said the platform would initially retain a two-business-day settlement cycle. He also said B3RL would not settle tokenized shares at launch, while round-the-clock trading would require changes to Brazil’s regulatory framework. The country’s Securities and Exchange Commission has been exploring tokenization rules and presented progress from its working group at an industry meeting in October.

data.title: Atoshi Router Proxy Contract Hit by Private-Key Theft; 201.05 Million ATOS Sold for $60,300
data.description: A private-key theft involving Atoshi’s router proxy contract on Ethereum is ongoing. According to Odaily, Blockaid reported that the attacker upgraded the active proxy to an implementation designed solely to transfer assets, then moved all ATOS held in the contract to a newly created wallet. About 201.05 million ATOS were sold on Kyber in roughly six transactions for about $60,300. The attack was still ongoing at the time of the report.

data.title: Bitcoin News | Bitcoin Short-Term Holders Sit on 15% Average Loss as STH MVRV Falls to 0.85, Near July Low
data.description: Bitcoin's short-term holder MVRV ratio has fallen to 0.85, almost matching its July low, CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost said in a post on Friday, November 27. The ratio peaked at 1.18 on September 22, when short-term holders were sitting on large profits, and stood at 0.81 on July 1.The MVRV ratio compares bitcoin's market value with its realized value, which prices each coin at the time it last moved. A reading below 1 means holders are, on average, at a loss. Darkfost estimates the short-term holder cost basis at $71,600, implying an average unrealized loss of about 15%."The market has returned to a difficult zone for short-term holders, who are currently holding Bitcoin at considerable losses," Darkfost said. He added that such levels "have historically coincided with bottom formation" and can offer opportunities for long-term investors.

data.title: US stock futures rally after Thanksgiving as AI-led tech rebound builds; Nasdaq 100 up 2.3%
data.description:
Bloomberg reported Friday that US stocks are set to rally strongly after the Thanksgiving break as the rebound in the AI trade gathers pace, with waning demand for havens sending Treasuries lower. Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 2.3%, building on Wednesday's late-session recovery, while S&P 500 contracts rose 1.7% and Dow futures added 1.3%. Nvidia advanced more than 3% in early trading as chipmakers jumped.

Europe's Stoxx 600 rose 1%, heading for its best week since May, and the MSCI Asia Pacific Index gained 1.8% after a rare midday statement outlining market-support measures in China lifted sentiment. Copper rallied as much as 6.5%, its biggest intraday jump since January; spot gold rose 3.1% to $3,677.53 an ounce; Bitcoin added 1.6% to $61,695.68 and Ether climbed 1.4% to $1,727.41.

Traders will watch whether the worst of the selling is over after weeks of unease over whether hundreds of billions of dollars in AI spending will pay off — the Nasdaq 100 was on course for its worst month since 2022 at Wednesday's close. Santiago Mateo at CaixaBank AM said the rebound can have staying power after the sharp correction, but the burden of proof has clearly increased, with the debate moving from AI adoption to whether deployed capital can generate adequate returns.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose five basis points to 4.90%. Brent crude added 0.2% to $96.74 a barrel, heading for its first weekly gain this month, as escalating attacks on Middle East energy infrastructure and tankers cast doubt on the durability of the crude supply rebound. Market pricing leans toward two further Fed hikes in 2027 after a December increase, but Mohit Kumar at Jefferies said next month should mark the peak in Fed hawkishness as inflation appears close to topping out.

Frederic Rozier at Mirabaud Asset Management said the move shows signs of a technical rebound with short-term upside potential after oversold conditions, while remaining prudent on the medium-to-longer term. Japan Tobacco climbed more than 4% as it explored a potential takeover of Imperial Brands with Altria; Qantas plans to award the bulk of an order for about 20 long-range jets to Boeing, and Acciona is weighing a merger back with its listed renewables unit.

data.title: China's Central Bank Pledges Ample Liquidity and Relatively Loose Financing Conditions
data.description: According to Jin10, the People's Bank of China released the China Financial Stability Report (2026), which says the financial system will flexibly and efficiently use various monetary policy tools to maintain ample liquidity and relatively loose social financing conditions. It will let the market play a decisive role in exchange-rate formation, maintain exchange-rate flexibility, guide expectations, and keep the RMB exchange rate basically stable at a reasonable and balanced level. The report also calls for coordinating work across the five major areas of finance, improving the policy framework for key areas including expanding domestic demand, technological innovation, and small and micro-sized enterprises, and improving the quality and effectiveness of financial services for high-quality development of the real economy. It calls for improving the comprehensive macroprudential management system, strengthening monitoring and assessment of systemic financial risks, and expanding the tools for macroprudential management and financial stability. It also calls for advancing the high-level opening of financial services and markets, strengthening financial risk prevention and control under an open framework, safeguarding national financial security, and continuing efforts to prevent and resolve risks in key areas by strictly controlling new risks, properly handling existing risks, preventing major risk events, and holding firmly to the bottom line of preventing systemic financial risks.

data.title: Nvidia Blackwell Chips Installed at Shanghai Data Center Linked to Alice Huang
data.description: Two Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, according to Bloomberg. Huang is at the center of a controversy involving the US chipmaker.

data.title: Goldman Sachs Warns Global Stocks Could Face About $100 Billion in Programmatic Selling Next Week
data.description:
Goldman Sachs warned that systematic trading funds could sell about $100 billion in global equities over the coming week, despite expectations of a rebound on Friday. According to Odaily, a trading team led by Paul Leyzerovich, head of Goldman Sachs’ trading desk, estimated that equity selling totaled about $70 billion over the past week and forecast a further $100 billion in selling over the coming week. The team said fund flows could turn to small net buying in early December.

After technology stocks came under pressure, trend-following funds and volatility-sensitive strategies remained defensively positioned. Goldman Sachs said selling pressure may persist in the short term, but a strong equity rebound could turn systematic trading flows into a source of market support in early December.

data.title: Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Rises 7.61%, Nearly Offsetting Previous Reduction
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing The Defiant, Bitcoin mining difficulty increased 7.61% in its latest adjustment, nearly offsetting the previous reduction. If Bitcoin’s price and block reward remain unchanged, miners are expected to earn about 7.1% less with the same hashrate.

data.title: Tether Adds About 3.72 Million Bitdeer Shares, Bringing Holdings to About 41.45 Million
data.description: Tether bought 3,715,943 Class A common shares of Bitcoin miner Bitdeer on the open market on Nov. 25. According to Foresight News, a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission shows the purchase was made in two transactions: 12,240 shares at $2.65 each and 3,703,703 shares at $2.693 each. After the purchase, Tether International held 41,445,453 Bitdeer Class A shares, representing 17.9% of the class’s total shares as of Sept. 30.

data.title: AI TRENDS | AI Takes More Than 90% of Venture Funding Growth as VC Funds Struggle to Exit
data.description: AI accounted for more than 90% of the increase in global venture funding in the third quarter, while established funds continued to face difficulties generating exits. According to PANews, global venture funding totaled $679 billion in 2026. As of June 30, the median distribution-to-paid-in capital ratio for U.S. venture funds from the 2017 vintage was 0.37x, and the listings of SpaceX and Anthropic had not led to observed share sales by venture funds.

data.title: JPMorgan Drops Forecast for 100-Basis-Point Turkish Rate Cuts in December and January
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, JPMorgan economist Fatih Akcelik said in a report on Friday that the bank no longer expects Turkey’s central bank to cut rates by 100 basis points in December and another 100 basis points in January, after it paused one-week repo auctions. JPMorgan expects the central bank to resume the auctions in February and restart its rate-cutting cycle in March.

JPMorgan expects the central bank to continue prioritizing foreign-exchange market stability and consider additional measures in the coming weeks to curb dollarization among Turkish residents. The report said the bank may also tighten its de-dollarization targets as an additional macroprudential measure, encouraging banks to raise interest rates on Turkish lira deposits.

JPMorgan expects Turkey’s consumer price index to rise 1.1% month over month in November, lifting annual inflation to 30.1% from 29.8% in October.
